Generated from the clap definition of the `modelspec` command line in [`crates/modelspec-cli/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-cli/src/lib.rs) by `modelspec-docs`. It lists only commands that exist.

> Compile, check, train and run .mspec models

`modelspec --version` prints its version, and `--help` after any command prints the text below.

## Exit status

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | success |
| `1` | diagnostics or a runtime error |
| `2` | a usage error |

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`modelspec check`](#modelspec-check) | Parse and type-check a `.mspec` file |
| [`modelspec infer`](#modelspec-infer) | Run the forward program of a `.mspec` model with the parameters of a checkpoint |
| [`modelspec inspect-device`](#modelspec-inspect-device) | Print the profile and negotiation verdict of each Vulkan physical device |
| [`modelspec ir`](#modelspec-ir) | Print the IR of a `.mspec` file at a stage |
| [`modelspec train`](#modelspec-train) | Train a `.mspec` model |

## `modelspec check`

Parse and type-check a `.mspec` file

```text
Usage: modelspec check <PATH>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | The .mspec file to check. |

## `modelspec infer`

Run the forward program of a `.mspec` model with the parameters of a checkpoint

```text
Usage: modelspec infer --backend <BACKEND> --checkpoint <PATH> <PATH>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | The .mspec file whose forward program runs. |
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | The backend that runs the forward program. One of:<br/>`cpu`: The CPU interpreter<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute on one device: `train` only, in a build with the vulkan feature |
| `--checkpoint <PATH>` | The .msckpt file whose parameters the forward program reads. |

## `modelspec inspect-device`

Print the profile and negotiation verdict of each Vulkan physical device

```text
Usage: modelspec inspect-device [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | yes | none | The backend whose devices are inspected. One of:<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute |
| `--device <INDEX>` | no | none | The index of one physical device, in the order the Vulkan loader lists them; without it every device is printed. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | `text` | The output format. One of:<br/>`text`: One `<field>: <value>` line per field, then the negotiation verdict<br/>`json`: The profile's JSON form, or a JSON array of profiles |

## `modelspec ir`

Print the IR of a `.mspec` file at a stage

```text
Usage: modelspec ir --stage <STAGE> <PATH>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | The .mspec file to lower. |
| `--stage <STAGE>` | The IR level to print. One of:<br/>`tensor`: Tensor IR after lowering and dead-code elimination<br/>`training`: Training IR: the Tensor IR with its reverse pass and SGD step attached<br/>`kernel`: Kernel IR: the kernels of the training step, its step plan and its forward plan |

## `modelspec train`

Train a `.mspec` model

```text
Usage: modelspec train [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND> <PATH>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | yes | none | The .mspec file to train. |
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | yes | none | The backend that runs the training step. One of:<br/>`cpu`: The CPU interpreter<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute on one device: `train` only, in a build with the vulkan feature |
| `--serve <ADDR>` | no | none | Stream the run's events as text/event-stream at path /events of ADDR, a loopback address such as 127.0.0.1:8080 or localhost:8080 (port 0 picks a free one); the process keeps serving after the run until SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, then exits with the run's status. |
| `--data <DIR>` | no | none | Train on the dense f32 files of DIR instead of synthetic data: NAME.f32 for the input and the target declaration NAME, row-major little-endian, and an optional order.u32 of sample indices. |
| `--init <DIR>` | no | none | Start each parameter that has a file DIR/P.f32, P its path without the model name, from that file instead of its initializer. |
| `--eval <DIR>` | no | none | After the last step, run the forward program over every sample of DIR, laid out as for --data, and print `eval loss=<mean loss> accuracy=<fraction>`. |
| `--steps <N>` | no | none | Run N steps instead of the steps of the file's train block; a resumed run ends at its checkpoint's step plus N. |
| `--checkpoint <PATH>` | no | none | After the last step, write the parameters, step and optimizer to the .msckpt file PATH. |
| `--checkpoint-every <N>` | no | none | Also write STEM-K.msckpt beside the --checkpoint file at every step K after the start that is a multiple of N and before the end. |
| `--resume <PATH>` | no | none | Continue from the .msckpt file PATH: its parameters and step instead of the initializers and step 0, refused unless it matches the compiled file and its optimizer. |
| `--device <INDEX>` | no | none | With --backend vulkan, train on the physical device INDEX, in the order the Vulkan loader lists them, instead of device 0. |
| `--stats` | no | `false` | With --backend vulkan, print the run's host waits, submits, dispatches, bytes copied up and down, numerics class and microseconds per step on stderr after it. |
| `--profile` | no | `false` | With --backend vulkan, time every dispatch with GPU timestamp queries and print one `profile dispatch` line per dispatch site, then the run's counters, compile and pipeline creation time and steady-state microseconds per step on stderr after it. |
